page.layout: One printed page, single column of text. Heading at top centred; then running text with a large woodcut initial M at the start of the first paragraph. Page number and catchword-like marks at the foot: "(?) (?) 3" and "Aucto-" at the lower right, which is a catchword.

main_text.l: Syllabus Auctorum, qui Annalibus his operam
suam commodârunt.
Manu-scripta.
Manu-scripta, quibus in his Annalibus usus sum,
sunt hæc sequentia:
Chronicon Levoldi à Northoff, nobilis Mar-
kani, Canonici Leodiensis & Abbatis sæcularis
Visetensis, qui sub Eberhardo Comite Marckano vixit, &
cum filio ejusdem Engelberto Romam, anno 1326. profe-
ctus est. Hoc Chronicon ex Latino barbaro in Westpha-
licum idioma convertit Ulricus Verne sacellanus Ham-
monensis: ex Westphalico in Germanicum purius Joan-
nes Kurtz / rationum Camerae Clivensis Magister: Lati-
nitate vero tertiori donavit, notisque suis eruditis illustra-
vit M. Henricus Meibomius Lemgoviensis, poëticês &
historiarum Professor in Academia Julia.
Chronicon Gerhardi Schurenij, sive ab Horreo dicti,
Sanctensis, Ducum Cliviae Adolphi Victoriosi & Joannis
bellicosi secretarius, in quo Principum Clivensium & Marc-
kensium originem atque progressum usque ad annum 1552.
deduxit, licet anno 1489. adhuc superstes fuerit. Ab anno
vero isto 1452. usque ad annum 1590. Johannes Lowerman
Emmericensis, Jurisconsultus & Wilhelmi Cliviae, Juliae,
Montium Ducis Consiliarius, inde Ioannes Turcus Go-
chensis Secretarius & Registrator Clivensis in praesens tem-
pus deduxerunt.
Chronicon aliud, in quo omnium Romanorum Impp.
Colon. Ultraject. Monast. Osnaburg. & Paderborn. Episco-
porum, omnium item Brabant. Holland. Flandr. Gelr. Cliv.
Jul. Mont. Marck. Ducum & Comitum res gestae parallelas
descriptae sunt, quod mihi ex Averdorpensi coenobio Vcsa-
llensi communicavit ejus quondam quaestor, vir multae
lectionis & antiquitatis in primis patriae studiosus Theodo-
ricus ab Uppich ὁ μαχαιρίτης.
Arnholdus Heimricius Clivensis, Decanus Sanctensis
in mss. variis, duobus tomis in Bibliotheca ejusdem Eccle-
siae extantibus.

page.notes: Woodcut initial M at the start of the first paragraph. Greek phrase after Uppich is printed in italic. Page number printed as "3" with "(?) (?)" marks to its left, likely signature or printer's marks; transcribed the page number only. Some words in the scan are faint or show-through; "Vcsallensi" and "Visetensis" are uncertain readings. The "Kurtz" line is in black letter.
